ai-at-work.title: Theker just raised $85M to build the factory robot that doesn’t specialize in anything
ai-at-work.excerpt: Unlike humanoid robots designed around a fixed form — think Boston Dynamics — Theker's machines are built to be reconfigured.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Theker landed 85 million dollars to develop generalist factory robots that can be reconfigured for different tasks rather than being locked into one specialized function. This matters because digital workplace teams are already stretched managing rigid, single-purpose enterprise systems, and flexible automation could eventually force a reckoning with how we design our own tools and workflows. The irony is thick: we're funding robots to be adaptable while most corporate software remains about as flexible as a brick.

ai-at-work.title: AI economics reshape FinOps as enterprises seek greater visibility and control
ai-at-work.excerpt: As AI spending accelerates across the enterprise, organizations are grappling with a new generation of cost and optimization challenges while seeking greater AI spend visibility. The next phase of Fin
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Enterprises are struggling to track and control mushrooming AI spending, pushing FinOps teams to build better visibility and accountability systems into their operations. This matters because digital workplace leaders now own a chunk of the AI bill, and without proper governance, departments will keep spinning up tools and models without anyone knowing what they cost or why. The real problem isn't AI itself, it's that we've finally met a technology expense category that makes our old budget meetings look quaint.

ai-at-work.title: Adobe beats expectations but another top executive leaves, putting pressure on its stock
ai-at-work.excerpt: A bad day for the creative software company Adobe Inc. was made even worse after it revealed another top executive is departing, as the news overshadowed a solid earnings and revenue beat. The company
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Adobe crushed its earnings targets but announced yet another executive departure, with CFO Dan Durn heading for the exits on June 15th. For digital workplace folks, this matters because Adobe's products are foundational to how creative teams work, and leadership instability can signal product direction uncertainty or internal friction that eventually trickles down to users. You can beat earnings all day long, but when your top people are leaving faster than employees on a Friday afternoon, investors and customers start asking the hard questions about what's really going on in the building.

ai-at-work.title: OpenAI acquires AI agent orchestration startup Ona
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to acquire Ona, a startup with a platform for managing long-running artificial intelligence agents. The terms of the deal were not disclosed. Developers often ru
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI bought Ona, a startup that manages long-running AI agents, to solve the problem of keeping AI systems running smoothly when developers aren't actively working. This matters because digital workplace leaders are about to get asked by every stakeholder how AI agents fit into their infrastructure, and now they need an actual answer about persistence and reliability. The real play here is that someone finally noticed the gap between flashy AI demos and the unglamorous work of keeping these things running without babysitting them constantly.

tools-tech.title: The cloud vs. clouded leopard: America's data center backlash on display at Nashville Zoo
tools-tech.excerpt: As fights against data centers spring up around the country, the latest showdown in Nashville has a furry face.
tools-tech.dwp_take: A Nashville Zoo campaign is using an endangered clouded leopard as the mascot for local opposition to a proposed data center expansion in the area. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals how communities are increasingly scrutinizing the real-world costs of cloud infrastructure, from land use to environmental impact to local power grids. Look, if your company's cloud strategy doesn't account for the fact that people are now literally putting endangered animals on billboards to fight data centers, you're not thinking far enough ahead.

tools-tech.title: Siri AI is all Apple; it just needed Google to get there
tools-tech.excerpt: Apple’s executives have been taking questions, hosting seminars, seemingly working around the clock to stress one very important thing: Apple is not using a white label version of Google Gemini to mak
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple spent considerable effort insisting its new Siri AI is homegrown, not just Google's Gemini repackaged, while simultaneously acknowledging a partnership that got them there faster. This matters because it reveals the dirty secret of enterprise AI: even the richest companies with the best engineers are partnering with competitors because building this stuff solo is slow and expensive. The real takeaway isn't whether Siri is "all Apple" but that we're entering an era where admitting you need help is somehow controversial.

tools-tech.title: Inside the coming war over face cameras
tools-tech.excerpt: Several trends are now converging that threaten to pit tech companies against tech users. Miniaturization has finally enabled companies to build AI glasses that look and function like normal glasses,
tools-tech.dwp_take: Companies are racing to build AI glasses with built-in cameras and microphones that look normal but record everything around you. This matters to digital workplace leaders because you'll suddenly need policies around whether employees can wear surveillance devices in meetings, what gets recorded, and who owns that data. Here's the thing though: we spent twenty years fighting shadow IT, and now we're about to fight shadow surveillance from people's own eyewear, which is going to be a compliance nightmare nobody's ready for.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft 365: A guide to the updates
tools-tech.excerpt: Microsoft 365 (and Office 365) subscribers get more frequent software updates than those who have purchased Office without a subscription, which means subscribers have access to the latest features, s
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft released a guide tracking the constant stream of updates flowing to M365 subscribers, which get fixes and features way faster than perpetual license buyers. For digital workplace folks, staying current on these updates matters because you're the ones fielding "why doesn't my Teams work like Sarah's Teams" calls from confused users. Honestly, the fact that we need a guide to track the updates to the tool we're supposed to be managing is pretty much Microsoft's business model in a nutshell.

digital-culture.title: What new mothers can teach us about the future of work
digital-culture.excerpt: If you want to know whether a workplace is built for the future, don’t ask the CEO. Ask the woman sprinting to daycare pickup at 5 pm. For the past several years we’ve approached new mothers as worker
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company published a piece suggesting that new mothers, rather than executives, are the real test of whether a workplace actually works for the future. The article argues we've been treating maternal support as a special accommodation rather than recognizing it as a lens for evaluating broader organizational flexibility and culture. Here's the thing: if your system only functions for people without competing demands, you've built a system that's fragile, inflexible, and honestly, already obsolete.

digital-culture.title: 13 career insurance policies every professional should have
digital-culture.excerpt: Today’s professional landscape demands more than technical skills and a polished resume. Career security now requires deliberate strategies that protect against disruption, position you as indispensab
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is telling you that job security isn't a thing anymore, so you need to build personal resilience through thirteen different strategies instead. This matters because digital workplace professionals operate in the fastest-changing environment of any sector, and what made you valuable last year might be obsolete next quarter. Look, I've seen entire skill sets disappear in five years, so yeah, thinking of career moves as "insurance policies" beats sitting around waiting for AI to make your job title irrelevant.

digital-culture.title: The rise of ‘doomjobbing’ reveals a hiring system nobody trusts
digital-culture.excerpt: There’s a word for aimlessly scrolling job ads without mustering the energy to apply to any of them. That word is “doomjobbing,” and it’s often fueled by the anxiety and uncertainty many workers are e
digital-culture.dwp_take: Workers are now "doomjobbing" - scrolling job listings endlessly without actually applying - because the job market feels so chaotic and unpredictable that even looking for work triggers anxiety. This matters because it signals a massive trust breakdown between employers and candidates, and your recruiting and HR teams need to understand that job seekers are burnt out before they even start. Honestly, if your company's job postings aren't compelling enough to snap someone out of doom-scrolling paralysis, that's a you problem, not a them problem.

digital-culture.title: The FDA just approved a new depression treatment—and it doesn’t involve medication
digital-culture.excerpt: Would you zap your brain to treat depression? In December, the Food and Drug Administration cleared a device that uses mild electrical currents to stimulate the brain, marking a shift in how the condi
digital-culture.dwp_take: The FDA approved a transcranial direct-current stimulation device for at-home depression treatment, marking the first non-medication option cleared for this use. Digital workplace leaders need to care because mental health infrastructure and employee support programs just got a new tool that could reshape how companies approach wellness benefits and remote worker mental health support. That said, I'm waiting to see the adoption data before anyone starts installing zapping stations in the office, because most companies are still struggling to get employees to use their existing EAP services.

industry-news.title: What is Revenue Operations? A Complete Guide
industry-news.excerpt: Learn what revenue operations is, how RevOps aligns sales, marketing, customer success, and finance, and how to build a RevOps function that supports predictable growth. The post What is Revenue Opera
industry-news.dwp_take: Revenue operations is basically the practice of aligning sales, marketing, customer success, and finance teams through shared data and processes to drive predictable growth. For digital workplace pros, this matters because RevOps success depends entirely on having solid collaboration tools, transparent workflows, and the kind of integrated platforms that actually let these departments talk to each other without sending stuff through three different systems. Honestly, if your organization can't get RevOps right, you've probably got bigger problems than your digital workplace tooling can fix, but don't let that stop you from trying.

industry-news.title: Google AI Overviews Legal Risks Raise New Enterprise Governance Questions
industry-news.excerpt: Google AI Overviews are facing legal and regulatory tests as companies consider how employees use AI search for research, compliance, and high-risk decisions. The post Google AI Overviews Legal Risks
industry-news.dwp_take: Google's AI Overviews are generating legal headaches because companies can't easily control how employees use them for research, compliance work, and critical decisions. This matters because digital workplace leaders now need governance policies for tools their workforce is already using, and they're flying blind without clear liability frameworks. Here's the thing: we spent decades locking down email and USB drives, and now everyone's dumping proprietary data into a search box that hallucinates citations. Same old problem in a shiny new package.

industry-news.title: New Apple Rumor: macOS 27 Hints at First Touchscreen Mac
industry-news.excerpt: macOS 27 beta features and supply chain rumors are fueling speculation that Apple may be preparing its first touchscreen MacBook. The post New Apple Rumor: macOS 27 Hints at First Touchscreen Mac appe
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple's apparently working on a touchscreen Mac based on macOS 27 beta clues and supply chain chatter. This matters because enterprises still bet heavily on Apple hardware, and touchscreen Macs could reshape how people expect to interact with their work devices. Personally, I've heard "the Mac will finally get touch" rumors since 2012, so I'll believe it when I'm swiping at my screen in actual production software.

industry-news.title: South Korea Drops a $409M Fine on Coupang in Historic Data Breach Ruling
industry-news.excerpt: South Korea fined Coupang $409 million after regulators said weak security controls led to a massive breach affecting 37.5 million accounts. The post South Korea Drops a $409M Fine on Coupang in Histo
industry-news.dwp_take: South Korea's regulators handed Coupang a $409 million fine for failing to secure customer data properly, with the breach exposing 37.5 million accounts. This matters because it shows regulators are finally putting real teeth into data protection enforcement and will hold even massive companies accountable for sloppy security practices. If your organization thinks compliance theater and half-baked security measures will fly, congratulations, you just met the cost of admission.
